methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - wtkr.com
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a local Norfolk native signal grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, directly targeting the technology gap through distributed peer learning rather than platform dependence.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education beyond NoVA, potentially seeding regional networks that could spread deep capability through Richmond's workforce rather than concentrating expertise.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents emerging capability in a traditionally non-tech region, but as a single institutional initiative it signals isolated excellence rather than distributed adoption—a pocket forming outside the NoVA-Richmond corridor.

signals.title: Virginia Tech secures $20m NSF grant for AI-enabled semiconductor lab - Cleanroom Technology
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's $20M NSF grant for AI-enabled semiconductor research deepens technical capacity in Blacksburg but concentrates cutting-edge capability in an academic hub, reinforcing the pattern of geographically clustered excellence rather than broad diffusion.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Severe electricity price hikes from data center infrastructure costs hitting civilian ratepayers statewide creates economic barriers that could inhibit distributed AI adoption, as communities bear concentration costs while benefits accrue to NoVA corporate clusters.
